title: TSMC overseas fabs see profit flip in 1H26, Arizona surges 663% YoY
gist: TSMC's four overseas subsidiaries combined for NT$58.53B profit in 1H26 (+215.4% YoY), with TSMC Arizona's profit surging 662.8% to overtake Nanjing as the largest foreign earnings contributor—evidence that geographic diversification is starting to pay off commercially, though rising depreciation costs and margin dilution warnings temper the bullish read.

insights.claim: TSMC's four foreign manufacturing subsidiaries generated a combined NT$58.53 billion in profit in the first half of 2026, up 215.4% year-on-year, marking an inflection point in the company's overseas manufacturing strategy.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: First clear evidence that TSMC's costly multi-year overseas expansion (US, Japan, China) is converting into profit rather than remaining a pure cost center, a key input for TSMC's margin trajectory and capital-allocation debate.
insights.quote: TSMC's overseas manufacturing strategy reached an inflection point in the first half of 2026, as all four foreign subsidiaries generated a combined NT$58.53 billion in profit, up 215.4% year on year.

insights.claim: TSMC Arizona's profit surged 662.8% year-on-year to NT$36.07 billion in 1H26, exceeding 60% of TSMC's total overseas profit and overtaking Nanjing as TSMC's largest foreign earnings contributor.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Arizona—long viewed as the highest-risk, highest-cost node of TSMC's overseas buildout due to labor and construction cost overruns—has flipped to become the profit leader among foreign fabs, a bullish datapoint for the US CHIPS Act investment thesis and for TSMC's US-based customers (Apple, Nvidia, AMD) betting on domestic capacity.
insights.quote: The standout was TSMC Arizona, whose profit surged 662.8% to NT$36.07 billion, exceeding 60% of the overseas total and overtaking Nanjing as the company's largest foreign earnings contributor.

insights.claim: Arizona's first fab runs 4-nanometer technology and is benefiting from strong AI/HPC chip demand, customer preference for US-based supply, and improving production efficiency.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Identifies three distinct demand/supply drivers (AI demand, geopolitical/customer preference for onshore supply, and operational learning curve) behind Arizona's turnaround—useful for modeling whether the improvement is durable or one-off.
insights.quote: Arizona's first fab, running 4-nanometer technology, is benefiting from strong demand for AI and high-performance computing chips, customer interest in US-based supply, and improving production efficiency.

insights.claim: Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing (JASM) swung from a loss in 1H25 to a NT$1.68 billion profit in 1H26, while Nanjing and Shanghai operations remained profitable throughout.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Shows the profitability turnaround is broad-based across TSMC's overseas footprint (Japan, China), not confined to Arizona alone, strengthening the case that global diversification overall is now accretive rather than dilutive.
insights.quote: Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing also moved from a first-half 2025 loss to a NT$1.68 billion profit, while the established Nanjing and Shanghai operations remained profitable.

themes.theme: Caveats: base effects, rising costs, and margin dilution

insights.claim: Arizona's headline 662.8% year-on-year profit growth is flattered by a low comparison base and should not be read as evidence the fab is now free of cost pressure.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A necessary discount factor for investors extrapolating Arizona's growth rate forward—the percentage gain overstates the durability of the improvement given how depressed the prior-year base was.
insights.quote: Still, the headline growth rate comes from a low comparison base and should not obscure rising costs.

insights.claim: Arizona's profit declined 8.2% sequentially in the second quarter of 2026 as depreciation and expansion expenses increased, even as the year-on-year comparison looked spectacular.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A sequential decline signals near-term cost pressure from continued capacity expansion (new fabs under construction) is already eating into Arizona's profit momentum quarter-to-quarter—an early warning sign against pure YoY-driven bullishness.
insights.quote: Arizona's second-quarter profit declined 8.2% sequentially as depreciation and expansion expenses increased.

insights.claim: TSMC has warned that its overseas expansion will dilute companywide gross margin by several percentage points.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Confirms that even as overseas subsidiaries individually turn profitable, TSMC's consolidated gross margin will structurally compress—critical for modeling TSMC's overall profitability, not just the overseas segment's standalone results.
insights.quote: TSMC has warned that overseas expansion will dilute companywide gross margin by several percentage points.

insights.claim: The durability of overseas returns depends on utilization rates, pricing, subsidies, execution, and whether AI demand stays strong enough to absorb an expanding global capacity base.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Lays out the explicit risk-monitoring checklist for the overseas-fab thesis: any softening in AI demand growth relative to TSMC's expanding global capacity would directly threaten these newly profitable subsidiaries' returns.
insights.quote: The results therefore validate overseas manufacturing commercially, but the durability of returns will depend on utilization, pricing, subsidies, execution, and whether AI demand remains strong enough to absorb an expanding global capacity base.
